exposure: maternal co-morbidities (PROM, polyhydramnios, diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, hypothyroidism)
cohort: The study included 150 healthy full-term neonates and their mothers.
finding: Male babies, babies born via LSCS, and babies born to mothers with hypothyroidism were significantly more prone to developing hyperbilirubinaemia in neonates.
mod_finding: Babies born via LSCS (Lower Segment Caesarean Section) were significantly more prone to developing hyperbilirubinaemia compared to those born via vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: A peripheral venous blood sample was drawn at the first significant clinical assessment of icterus or at 72 hours of life.
gest_age: Full-term neonates (mean 38.4 weeks overall, 38.1 weeks in hyperbilirubinaemic babies)
